title: Horizon Pay POC — Performance Playbook (latency / throughput / cost)
summary: End-to-end benchmarking summary for Horizon Pay fraud-detection LLM POC. Compares hosted vs dedicated vs private in latency, throughput, and estimated unit cost. Includes test matrix, key results, recommendations, and next steps.
content:
Purpose and context:

This doc captures the benchmarks run for Horizon Pay's fraud-detection POC (internal codename: HP-PoC). Goal: validate that Redwood can meet Horizon's SLA targets (p50 <= 40ms for single-turn inference, p99 <= 200ms under typical burst traffic), sustain required throughput (10k reqs/minute steady, 18k/min peak), and achieve competitive per-1M-token economics for the customer workload. Tests compare three deployment modes: Redwood Hosted API (multi-tenant), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Redwood Private (VPC deployment in customer cloud).

Test environment and constraints:
- Test date range: 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-16.
- Models tested: small-med transformer variant (hp-lite-7b-fp16) and quantized 4-bit candidate (hp-lite-7b-q4). Both are causally masked encoder-decoder style prompts tuned for short-context scoring and short completions (avg output length 24 tokens).
- Hardware: Dedicated runs on DGX-class instances (A100 80GB equiv), Private runs on customer c5g + local A10p cluster (provided by Horizon), Hosted runs on mixed GPU pool (NVIDIA H100 + A100 fallback).
- Batching policy: continuous batching enabled for Dedicated/Private; Hosted used standard Redwood adaptive batching. We tested batch sizes {1, 4, 8, 16} where applicable.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching exercised for repeated session tokens (session reuse ratio estimated 22%).
- Quantization runs: baseline fp16 vs q4. We measured quality regressions using a small eval suite of 120 production-like prompts (precision-sensitive fraud heuristics).
- Traffic profiles: three synthetic profiles: steady (10k/min), spiky (baseline 5k/min with 3x bursts up to 20k/min), and chatty (longer sessions with multiple calls/session). Traffic generated from our internal load generator across two regions (us-west1, us-east1).

Key metrics captured (per-run):
- p50, p90, p95, p99 latency (ms) end-to-end (client -> response last token).
- Throughput (requests per minute), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, average batch size.
- Cost estimate: compute cost driven by GPU utilization and reserved pricing; additional egress/infra costs estimated for Private. Reported as $ per 1M tokens (in USD).

Results — highlights (concise):
- Hosted (mixed pool, adaptive batching): p50=28ms, p99=210ms under steady 10k/min for hp-lite-7b-fp16. Under spiky profile p99 rose to 420ms during bursts due to fallbacks to older A100 nodes. Average cost: $18 / 1M tokens (includes rate-limited autoscale overhead).
- Dedicated (reserved DGX-class pool, continuous batching): p50=22ms, p99=95ms steady; sustained 18k/min with p99 <= 130ms under spiky bursts. Average cost: $9 / 1M tokens (amortized reserved capacity).
- Private (Horizon infra, A10p cluster, local autoscale): p50=30ms, p99=140ms steady; p99 spikes to ~260ms when noisy neighbor IO peaks on the customer cluster. Observed additional tail from network serialization in VPC. Estimated cost: $11 / 1M tokens (includes infra amortization, ops overhead).
- Quantization (q4) reduced average token cost by ~28% on Dedicated and Private with small quality delta: 97% parity on fraud-rule precision, 94% parity on subtle semantic flags. Hosted quantized runs were occasionally routed to non-quantization-ready nodes causing increased variance; needs routing policy.

Detailed observations and anomalies:
- Batch-size sensitivity: For hp-lite-7b-fp16, throughput improved linearly up to batch=8; batch=16 produced diminishing returns for latency-sensitive 95/99 metrics. Continuous batching on Dedicated allowed larger effective batch sizes without p99 degradation.
- KV/prefix caching: Workload with 22% session reuse saw ~30% drop in token compute on Dedicated when caching enabled; caching on Hosted reduced cost but was less consistent due to routing across pools.
- Fallbacks: Hosted fallback policy (H100 -> A100 -> CPU) caused p99 cliff during rare capacity pressure; recommend explicit fallback to quantized variant in policy for this customer to protect SLA.
- Private infra IO: Horizon's A10p nodes share NVMe on host. During nightly backups we observed IO-induced jitter causing p99 tail inflation; ops correlation showed backups aligned with 02:00-03:00 daily.

Quality tradeoffs (q4 vs fp16):
- Evaluated on fraud-eval-120: average fraud-detection precision (binary classifier like scoring) dropped 2.4 percentage points on q4; recall unchanged. For their risk-tolerance this is acceptable for non-blocking score tier but not for final actioning.
- Recommendation: use q4 for pre-screening/score-first path; route high-risk or borderline requests to fp16 path (can be a separate route in Redwood).

Cost modeling (high-level):
- Assumptions: avg output length 24 tokens, input avg 18 tokens. Tokenization rates consistent across models.
- Hosted rough: $18 / 1M tokens (observed) -> monthly estimate for 50M tokens = $900. Hosted variability expected at scale and with burst tolerance add-ons.
- Dedicated reserved: $9 / 1M tokens -> monthly estimate for same = $450. Includes reserved pool amortization and basic support.
- Private: $11 / 1M tokens -> monthly estimate $550 (higher ops + networking overhead).

Operational recommendations for Horizon POC:
1) Start with Dedicated for the remainder of the POC: meets latency and p99 targets, better cost predictability.
2) Roll quantized model (q4) as a second-class fast path for pre-scoring; set threshold to re-run fp16 path for scores within 0.15 margin. Implement via Redwood route policy (fast-path q4, fallback fp16).
3) Add explicit routing policy to Hosted pool to prefer quantization-ready nodes for quantized variants; otherwise prefer Dedicated for production.
4) For Private deployment: advise Horizon on NVMe backup scheduling or node isolation to avoid nightly backups during business hours; consider dedicated storage partition or adjust backup windows.
5) Instrument additional synthetic spike tests (up to 30k/min) during next on-site workshop to validate graceful degradation and autoscale timings.

Action items / next steps (owners and rough ETA):
- SE: implement route policy PR for q4 fast path and fp16 fallback (owner: Liam Chen) — ETA: 2026-07-28.
- SRE: add synthetic spike harness to run 30k/min stress test and collect tracing; validate autoscale cold-start (owner: SRE Team) — ETA: 2026-07-30.
- Solutions Eng + Horizon Ops: schedule 2-hr workshop to review Private infra IO findings and agree mitigation (owner: Marisol Gutierrez / Horizon Ops) — ETA: 2026-07-24.
- Research: run expanded quality eval (1k prompts) to characterize q4 edge cases (owner: Devon Patel) — ETA: 2026-07-31.

Open questions and risks:
- Long-tail quality: will q4 produce more subtle false positives in live traffic than the 120-sample eval shows? (Mitigation: staged rollout + telemetry and rollback).
- Hosted cold-fallbacks: how often will customer hit non-quantization nodes in real traffic pattern? (Mitigation: prefer Dedicated, or pin quantization-ready nodes to account tier).
- Private ops: Horizon must commit to storage IO scheduling guarantees or choose node types with isolated NVMe.

Appendix: quick test matrix (abbreviated)
- Run A (Hosted, fp16, steady 10k/min): p50=28ms, p99=210ms, cost=~$18/1M
- Run B (Dedicated, fp16, steady 10k/min): p50=22ms, p99=95ms, cost=~$9/1M
- Run C (Dedicated, q4, steady 10k/min): p50=18ms, p99=104ms, cost=~$6.5/1M, quality delta -2.4pp precision
- Run D (Private, fp16, steady 10k/min): p50=30ms, p99=140ms, cost=~$11/1M

Notes to self (informal):
- Customer cares most about p99 under burst and predictable monthlies — highlight Dedicated economics in follow-up deck.
- Need a short one-pager for Horizon execs showing expected SLOs vs cost tradeoffs (two slide options: Dedicated-first vs Hosted-cost-smoothing).
- Slack threads: #hp-poc-bench (see linked artifacts) has more raw logs and flamegraphs.

Contact for questions: Aisha Kapoor (aisha@redwood.ai) — ping for raw run artifacts or to schedule on-site runbook review.

End of doc.
